title: Sunset and moonset
caption: Sunset and moonset over Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Soon after sunset, the last light of day glows as an orange haze over ESO's Paranal Observatory, colored as it passes through the dusty lower atmosphere. Toward the lower left, a crescent Moon slowly sets, seeming to sink into the Pacific Ocean, while star trails cross the darkening sky.

This is a long-exposure composite. The trails look a bit like dotted lines because several separate shots, with short gaps between them, were combined. They bend at the bottom where the camera shifted out of place. The Moon, by contrast, is not trailed, because it was captured with a series of very short exposures.
Other visitors crossed the scene too. A meteor appears as a vertical streak in the center, and the blinking lights of planes track horizontally across the sky.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based composite of several long exposures for the star trails and a series of very short exposures for the Moon, by Gabriel Brammer. The source does not publish color-processing details.
understand.eye: An observer would see stars as points and the Moon as a single crescent. The combined exposures turn the stars into dotted trails and the Moon into a sequence along its path.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: ESO Photo Ambassador Gabriel Brammer took the picture while working as an astronomer at the La Silla-Paranal Observatory. It was one of his very first night shots of Paranal and is still among his favorites. He later moved to the Space Telescope Science Institute in Maryland, USA, to support the Hubble Space Telescope.
alt: An observatory on a mountain under an orange sunset haze, with dotted star trails, a setting crescent Moon at lower left, a vertical meteor streak and horizontal plane lights.
